hostile_review_findings.title: Refusal artifact accepted a backdated evaluation stamp under the signed rights registry
hostile_review_findings.mechanism: event_ledger.verify_payload_bytes derives the evaluation instant from the payload's own _meta.generated, then recomputes build(evaluated_at=that) and byte-compares. Under the founder's signed 2026-08-15 registry, _meta.generated is the ONLY field that varies with evaluated_at (measured by building at two instants and diffing every leaf), so a backdated stamp reproduces itself byte-for-byte and the comparison cannot see it.
hostile_review_findings.bounded_severity: Forward-dating was always refused (refusal_evaluation_time_future). No field other than _meta.generated can be forged; the byte comparison still covers them. The open window was backdating from contract_effective to now -- four days on 2026-08-16, widening each day the contract-effective date recedes. It is a freshness lie in a value-free refusal artifact, not arbitrary content forgery.
hostile_review_findings.why_the_checkpoint_missed_it: It PASSES at 2f4d4264. The checkpoint's own rights state left another field varying with evaluation time, so the recomputation caught the tamper. The weakness appears only once real signatures land -- the configuration that actually ships. Neither H0's tests nor CI would have caught it.
hostile_review_findings.remediation: verify_payload_bytes now bounds the evaluation stamp by the already-registered MAX_REFUSAL_RELEASE_AGE when release_instant is None; the release path already enforced the same bound through release_instant.
hostile_review_findings.deadlock_check: Both callers verify the current artifact, never a historical one, and --verify-payload is wired into no workflow (CI runs only --check). A freshness bound on a historical verifier would have rebuilt the transition-deadlock pattern; it does not here.
hostile_review_findings.regression_tests: tests/test_event_ledger_backdating.py -- 6 tests pinning both edges plus the mechanism itself. Proven to bite: fix stashed, 2 fail; restored, 6 pass.

hostile_review_findings.title: H0 requires a public schema copy that exists in no commit of the lineage
hostile_review_findings.mechanism: src/endpoint_unavailable.py declares DOCS_SCHEMA_RELATIVE = docs/schemas/endpoint-unavailable.schema.json and the publish path requires it to exist and be byte-identical to the root schemas/ copy, refusing endpoint_unavailable_schema_bytes_mismatch otherwise. The checkpoint shipped the root copy and the code demanding both, but never the docs copy.
hostile_review_findings.evidence: The same tests fail identically at 2f4d4264 on its own parent 4c4eec49. The path is absent at 4c4eec49, 2f4d4264, c363af12 and eb050bd5.
hostile_review_findings.remediation: Added byte-identical; sha256 18da4675a4e68c93418b94384616c2bdaec2712b91c1a1935fb5a570042775d6 matches the code's PINNED_SCHEMA_SHA256.

hostile_review_findings.title: The publisher's decision-signature pin does not know the founder's 2026-08-15 decisions
hostile_review_findings.mechanism: src/endpoint_unavailable.py iterates every approved registry row and requires each row's signature digest in PINNED_DECISION_SIGNATURE_SHA256, which holds exactly one entry (the ngrams aggregate decision). The two rows approved on 2026-08-15 -- gdelt_doc_api and gdelt_bq_webngrams -- have no pin, so publish_final_cas.sh refuses with endpoint_unavailable_decision_signature_invalid.
hostile_review_findings.signature_verification_performed: All three approved decisions were verified as 64-byte Ed25519 signatures over the exact committed artifact bytes under the enrolled, unrevoked human:igrm-ngram-rights-reviewer key, with each artifact digest matching its registry row. All three VALID.
hostile_review_findings.why_claude_did_not_complete_it: Registering the two pins requires coordinated edits across five anchors: the constant in src/endpoint_unavailable.py, PUBLIC_TREE_HELPER_SHA256 in src/security_integrity.py, the security registry entry, and a hard-coded git blob OID (aa00529c74592a3001ce87157bfb6105a59ac595) embedded twice in each of scripts/publish_final_cas.sh and scripts/ship.sh -- both themselves sha-pinned publisher scripts. That multi-anchor design exists so no single automated actor can quietly widen what the publisher trusts. A trial edit was made, verified to move the refusal forward one layer, and then REVERTED so no half-registered state was frozen; src/endpoint_unavailable.py is back at its exact H0 bytes (digest 442cb0ad).
